A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of pretrained attention matrices and training experiments with 4- and 12-layer language models, including initialization comparisons in Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds 24-layer language-model experiments and vision-transformer experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1k.

M1.justification: The applied symmetric initializer remains Wk = Wq, including its vision application. However, Appendix S2.1 removes v1's optional skew-symmetric initializer and symmetry/skew-symmetry loss penalties, narrowing the described method variants. This does not establish a procedural change in the retained experiments.

E1.justification: New Appendix S3 extends initialization training and evaluation to image classification on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1k. v1 already analyzed pretrained vision-model weights, but did not report these image-classification experiments. The three language-training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Both versions compare symmetric initialization against standard independent initialization; the added experiments retain this comparator. The pretrained-model comparison tables also retain the same model membership.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 24-layer BERT configuration and separate 6- and 12-layer ViT protocols, including 500/200 training epochs, image augmentation, cosine scheduling, weight averaging, and evaluation loss/top-1 accuracy. These are protocols for added experiments; the existing language-model training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The layerwise, headwise, and initialization-dynamics analyses in Figures 3 and S3-S5 are retained. Added BERT-Large and ViT benchmark results extend the existing initialization comparison without introducing a distinct ablation variable, sensitivity sweep, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report medians and interquartile ranges across layers or heads for structural analyses. Neither provides training-run counts, seeds, or run-level uncertainty for initialization comparisons; the new training results are also point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds 24-layer standard/symmetric losses of 0.786/0.739 on Jigsaw, 0.192/0.166 on Wikipedia, and 0.209/0.189 on Red Pajama, with reported speed-ups of 14%, 44%, and 34%. New Table S3 reports ViT accuracies of 0.90/0.89 on CIFAR-10 and 0.76/0.76 on ImageNet-1k. Existing language-result rows, pretrained-model scores, and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Beyond relocating existing propositions and theorems, v2 removes the asserted bidirectional joint-probability factorization and adds DAG/pseudolikelihood reasoning in S1.3. Remark S1.10 introduces an expected-position bound, while S1.5.5-S1.5.6 substantially revise the directionality and equal-norm derivations, including the column/row variance ordering. Equation (3) also changes from normalized attention weights to raw scores.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and discussion retain the same central claims: autoregressive training induces directionality, bidirectional training induces symmetry, and symmetric initialization benefits language-model training. Additional experiments support or qualify these claims without redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix S3 interprets symmetric initialization as offering little benefit for the tested ViTs and explicitly leaves other vision configurations open. This adds a concrete applicability boundary absent from v1's more general call for research across domains.

D1.justification: v2 supplies BERT-Large specifications and a substantial reproduction recipe for the new vision experiments: architecture configurations, patch sizes, optimizer settings, schedules, batch sizes, augmentation parameters, label smoothing, and weight-averaging settings. The existing language-training recipe and code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Besag and XLNet references for pseudolikelihood, together with references supporting CIFAR-10, ImageNet, mixup, CutMix, and weight averaging. Section 5's mechanistic-interpretability positioning and relationship to mimetic initialization remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The central theoretical exposition is substantially rewritten and reorganized. Section 2 separates context/prediction effects from objective-specific consequences, recasts the geometric proposition as prose, and promotes appendix statements into the main text. The proof appendix gains a roadmap, explicit assumption lists, and reorganized derivations, while the abstract and discussion remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a 24-layer block, Table S1 gains a BERT-Large column, and new Tables S2-S3 present ViT configurations and results. Existing figure artwork is retained, with caption edits and redistribution across pages; the overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The larger language-model experiment, informative vision null results, and detailed configurations improve empirical scope and reproducibility. The pseudolikelihood correction and clearer assumptions also help. However, the rewrite introduces inconsistencies, including raw attention scores in Equation (3) and an autoregressive objective in the bidirectional Corollary S1.12, while new results lack run-level uncertainty. The evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than a substantial strengthening.
